        arxiv_bigram_tokens.update(zip(toks_title, toks_title[1:]))
        text_lower = (title + " " + summary).lower()
        for kw in arxiv_keywords:
            if kw in text_lower:
                arxiv_entities[kw]+=1

]

pattern_cache = {kw: re.compile(r'\b'+re.escape(kw)+r'\b') for kw in arxiv_kw2}

with open(arxiv_data_path,"r") as f:
    for line in f:
        rec = json.loads(line)
        pub = rec.get("published","")
        if not pub.startswith("2025-11-"):
            continue
        text = (rec.get("title","") + " " + rec.get("summary","")).lower()
        for kw, pat in pattern_cache.items():
            if pat.search(text):
                arxiv_keyword_counts[kw]+=1

Parsing Reddit threads for trending topics
import re, textwrap

# Let's parse reddit threads quickly
thread_pattern = re.compile(r"--- THREAD: (.*?) ---\n(.*?)(?=\n--- THREAD: |\Z)", re.DOTALL)
threads = []
for m in thread_pattern.finditer(reddit_text):
    title = m.group(1).strip()
    body = m.group(2).strip()
    # extract subreddit and comments
    m2 = re.search(r"Subreddit:\s*([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*\|.*?Comments:\s*(\d+)", body)
    subreddit = m2.group(1) if m2 else None
    comments_count = int(m2.group(2)) if m2 else None
    # get text after 'POST:' and maybe comment content as well
    post_match = re.search(r"POST:(.*?)(?:\n\nCOMMENTS:|\Z)", body, re.DOTALL)
    post_text = post_match.group(1).strip() if post_match else ""
    # note: comments not extracted; but we could later
    threads.append({
        "title": title,
        "subreddit": subreddit,
        "comments": comments_count,
        "post": post_text,
    })

len(threads), threads[0]

import json, collections, re, itertools, datetime, math, statistics, html

blog_sources = collections.Counter()
blog_titles = []
blog_dates = []
blog_source_examples = collections.defaultdict(list)

with open(blog_path) as f:
    for i, raw in enumerate(f):
        raw = raw.strip()
        if not raw:
            continue
        try:
            obj = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        src = obj.get("sourceId") or obj.get("source") or "unknown"
        blog_sources[src] += 1
        if len(blog_source_examples[src]) < 3:
            blog_source_examples[src].append(obj.get("title","")[:200])
        if i < 200:
            blog_titles.append(obj.get("title","")[:200])
        # collect dates
        dt_str = obj.get("publishedAt") or obj.get("date") or obj.get("published_at")
        if dt_str:
            try:
                blog_dates.append(datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(dt_str.replace("Z","+00:00")))
            except Exception:
                pass

Designing entity extraction for blog data analysis
import json, datetime, re, collections, math, statistics, html

blog_path = "/mnt/data/manual_kit/manual_kit/data/blogs/all_blogs.txt"
now = datetime.datetime(2025,11,25,tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)

def strip_html(text):
    # simple HTML tag removal
    text = re.sub(r"<script.*?</script>", " ", text, flags=re.S|re.I)
    text = re.sub(r"<style.*?</style>", " ", text, flags=re.S|re.I)
    text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", text)
    return html.unescape(text)

# definitions for hype vs substance keywords
HYPE_WORDS = set("""
revolutionary transformative groundbreaking unprecedented magical
seamless delightful amazing incredible game-changing disruptive
paradigm-shift empower empowering frictionless visionary
""".split())
SUBSTANCE_WORDS = set("""
throughput latency benchmark accuracy mmlu human-eval humaneval
tokens-per-second tps parameters flops gflops tflops api docs
documentation reproducible dataset open-source opensource weights
checkpoint inference fine-tune finetune evaluation ablation
""".split())

# Entities candidate regex
entity_pattern = re.compile(r"\b([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.+-]{2,})\b")

blog_stats = {
    "total_posts": 0,
    "source_counts": collections.Counter(),
    "year_counts": collections.Counter(),
    "posts_recent": 0,
    "posts_breaking": 0,
    "posts_last7": 0,
    "new_items": [],
    "update_items": [],
    "resurfaced_items": [],
    "research_spotlights": [],
    "strategic_signals": [],
    "source_examples": collections.defaultdict(list),
    "source_hype_substance": collections.defaultdict(lambda: {"hype":0,"sub":0,"tokens":0}),
    "entity_counts": collections.Counter(),
    "entity_post_counts": collections.Counter(),
}

# heuristics keywords
NEW_KEYWORDS = ["introducing","announcing","announce","launching","launch","is here","now available","coming soon","general availability","GA","new "]
UPDATE_KEYWORDS = ["update","updated","improved","improving","adds support","now supports","v2","v3","2.0","3.0","beta","preview","rc"]
RESURFACE_KEYWORDS = ["retrospective","two years","years of","anniversary","revisiting","flashback"]

def classify_temporal(dt):
    delta = now - dt
    days = delta.total_seconds()/86400.0
    if days <= 1.0:
        bucket = "breaking"
    elif days <= 7.0:
        bucket = "last7"
    else:
        bucket = "older"
    return bucket, days

# run single pass limited to maybe 400 posts to keep speed? but we might want all.
# Let's try full but keep per-post text handling limited (e.g., for hype/substance we only use title+first 1000 chars).
import time
start_time = time.time()

with open(blog_path) as f:
    for raw in f:
        raw = raw.strip()
        if not raw:
            continue
        try:
            obj = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        blog_stats["total_posts"] += 1
        src = obj.get("sourceId") or obj.get("source") or "unknown"
        blog_stats["source_counts"][src] += 1
        if len(blog_stats["source_examples"][src]) < 5:
            blog_stats["source_examples"][src].append(obj.get("title","")[:200])
        dt_str = obj.get("publishedAt") or obj.get("date") or obj.get("published_at")
        dt = None
        if dt_str:
            try:
                dt = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(dt_str.replace("Z","+00:00"))
            except Exception:
                # try parse YYYY-MM-DD
                m = re.match(r"(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})", dt_str)
                if m:
                    try:
                        dt = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(m.group(1)+"T00:00:00+00:00")
                    except Exception:
                        dt = None
        if dt:
            blog_stats["year_counts"][dt.year] += 1
            bucket, days = classify_temporal(dt)
            if bucket == "breaking":
                blog_stats["posts_breaking"] += 1
            if bucket in ("breaking","last7"):
                blog_stats["posts_last7"] += 1
        title = obj.get("title") or ""
        content = obj.get("content") or obj.get("summary") or ""
        # Limit content processed for speed
        plain = (title + " " + strip_html(content))[:2000].lower()
        tokens = re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z0-9_.+-]+", plain)
        if tokens:
            blog_stats["source_hype_substance"][src]["tokens"] += len(tokens)
        for tok in tokens:
            if tok in HYPE_WORDS:
                blog_stats["source_hype_substance"][src]["hype"] += 1
            if tok in SUBSTANCE_WORDS:
                blog_stats["source_hype_substance"][src]["sub"] += 1
        # entity extraction from title only (more precise)
        for ent in set(entity_pattern.findall(title)):
            # filter generic words
            if ent.lower() in ("the","and","with","from","into","your","this","that","open","data","ai","ml","deep","neural","network","analysis","learning","research","update","blog"):
                continue
            blog_stats["entity_counts"][ent] += 1
            blog_stats["entity_post_counts"][ent] += 1

end_time = time.time()
summary = {
    "total_posts": blog_stats["total_posts"],
    "num_sources": len(blog_stats["source_counts"]),
    "top_sources": blog_stats["source_counts"].most_common(10),
    "year_counts": blog_stats["year_counts"],
    "posts_breaking": blog_stats["posts_breaking"],
    "posts_last7": blog_stats["posts_last7"],
    "elapsed_sec": round(end_time-start_time,2)
}

Handling temporal gaps in blog data

It looks like there was a mix-up with timestamps: our "now" is set to November 25, 2025, but the most recent post was published on November 19, 2025. That makes posts within 24 hours impossible. For analysis, posts from the last 7 days still have value, and older posts are grouped accordingly. We might mention the gap as a data quality issue.

Balancing substance and hype in blog data

The ratio of substance to hype is about 0.127 — so the content is more focused on substance, with limited hype vocabulary. To refine this, I’ll calculate the hype-to-substance ratio per source, making sure to filter out smaller datasets (sources with less than 500 tokens) to avoid skewing results.

Computing source hype-to-substance ratios 
source_hype_ratio = []
for src, hs in blog_stats["source_hype_substance"].items():
    if hs["tokens"] < 500:
        continue
    hype = hs["hype"]
    sub = hs["sub"] or 1
    ratio = hype/sub
    source_hype_ratio.append((ratio, src, hype, sub, hs["tokens"]))
# sort descending ratio
source_hype_ratio = sorted(source_hype_ratio, reverse=True)[:10]
